items.title: Cosimo Matassa Interview, 1993-07-17
items.q: You remember he did Walking with Mr. Lee?

ctx.x: All right, reel number four, Cosmo Matanza, July 17th, 1993. Okay, we're going to continue on. No, we're going through the record companies, some of the early record companies that came to New Orleans, and we were talking about Imperial, Imperial Records. But Imperial would come here, and of course, with the first hits of Fats Domino, would of course have a long stay in New Orleans.

Yeah, well, I think Fats did something like 20 gold records in a row. Sure. It was phenomenal. But that, of course, opened the door for lots of other people, and it brought other people here, too. And you've got to remember now, Imperial wasn't the first company to come down. We talked about Deluxe and Apollo, and what was the guy in New Jersey had a label? I'm trying to think of it. You remember he did Walking with Mr. Lee?
That's Al Silvers. Yeah, but what time was his last name?
